description: Control-plane JSON vectors: the preamble/mode-branch handshake, the outer LinkWireFrame, the LinkEnvelope, and the LinkMessage set. See ProjectInfo/04-PROTOCOL.md sections 4-6.
derivation: Derived from the declared field names and the normative codec settings, not captured from either implementation.
orderingNote: JSON objects are unordered, and the frame MAC is computed over the bytes as received rather than over a re-serialization, so member order is NOT a correctness requirement and these vectors do not pin it. What they do pin is the exact set of keys produced, the discriminator values, that defaults ARE emitted, and that nulls are OMITTED rather than written as null.
nullPolicyNote: explicitNulls = false means an absent optional field is omitted entirely. A peer emitting "reason": null instead of omitting it is a conformance bug, even though a tolerant parser would accept it.

handshakeVectors.name: LinkPreamble
handshakeVectors.note: encodeDefaults = true, so platform and protocolVersion appear even when left at their defaults. LINK_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 2 since ADR-031; pair and pk are null by default and therefore omitted.

handshakeVectors.name: LinkPreamble for confirm pairing
handshakeVectors.note: 04-PROTOCOL.md 4.3. pk is the sender's static X25519 public key, standard base64 with padding.

handshakeVectors.name: LinkPreambleAck for confirm pairing
handshakeVectors.note: Values from pair-confirm.json: pkB and the commitment C.

handshakeVectors.name: pairNonce
handshakeVectors.note: Unauthenticated text frame, not inside a LinkWireFrame. n is 32 bytes, base64 (nA from pair-confirm.json).

wireFrameVectors.name: Session-mode frame carries c, not p
Pairing-mode frame carries p, not c

messageVectors.name: hello
messageVectors.note: capabilities and maxChunk are defaults and must still be emitted.

messageVectors.name: pairOk
messageVectors.note: This message carries the long-lived session secret and is always sent sealed, never in the clear.

messageVectors.name: offer
messageVectors.note: senderWifiP2pAddress is null and must be omitted. preferredRoutes is the ordered route preference used by ADR-023.

messageVectors.name: offer of a folder
messageVectors.note: ADR-064, sent only to a peer with FOLDER_TRANSFER (0x0002). Every path starts with the folder's name. Files come first; then each empty directory as an item with isDir true and size 0, which is offered but never streamed. totalBytes counts the files only.

messageVectors.name: decision accepting over LAN_TCP
messageVectors.note: Every optional field that is null must be omitted. authToken is the ephemeral per-transfer credential for the VTC1 socket.

messageVectors.name: decision with a resume map
messageVectors.note: resume maps itemIndex to the chunk indices still needed. Absent means send everything.

messageVectors.name: chunk fallback
messageVectors.note: Base64 in JSON. Correct but slow; the normal path is the VTC1 raw TCP data plane.

forwardCompatibilityVectors.name: An unknown key inside a known message must be ignored, not rejected
forwardCompatibilityVectors.note: This is what lets a newer peer add a field without breaking an older one. Rejecting here would make every future field a breaking change.

forwardCompatibilityVectors.name: An unknown key inside the envelope must be ignored
An unknown discriminator must be rejected, not silently ignored
forwardCompatibilityVectors.note: Unknown FIELDS are forward compatibility; an unknown MESSAGE TYPE is not something a v1 peer can act on, and guessing would be worse than refusing.

notes: The preamble is unauthenticated and carries no authority. It exists so the receiver can decide which key to use; the mode decision that follows is what grants anything.
pairOk is always sealed even though pairing mode is nominally plaintext, because it carries the session secret. There is no plaintext fallback and therefore no downgrade path.
Adding a nullable field with a null default is not a breaking change and does not require a VLP_VERSION bump. Removing a field or changing its meaning does.
